chunks: Abu Basir narrated from him, peace be upon him.
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
For you, there are benefits in them until a specified term.
He said: If one needs its back, he may ride it without being harsh upon it. And if it has milk, he may milk it in a manner that does not exhaust it.

key_terms.أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: a specified term, meaning the fixed appointed time
key_terms.حِلَابًا: milking, meaning the act of drawing milk
key_terms.ظَهْرِهَا: its back, referring to riding the animal
key_terms.مَنَافِعُ: benefits or useful advantages derived from the animal
key_terms.يَعْنُفَ: to be harsh or rough in treatment
key_terms.يَنْهَكُهَا: to wear it out or exhaust it

ai.seo_question: Can a sacrificial animal be ridden or milked before it is offered?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic verse as permitting benefit from sacrificial animals before the appointed time. Such benefit is allowed within limits of mercy and moderation, so the animal is neither treated harshly nor exhausted.
